content.text:
I fixed the panic in `float_split` in `crates/syntax-bridge/src/lib.rs`. I haven't confirmed the fix on your example, because I didn't run it or add a test for it.

**Cause:** `00E+10` is a float literal with no `.`. The parser accepts it as a field access and reports an "illegal float literal" error. The syntax bridge assumed every such literal contained a `.` and hit `unreachable!()` when it didn't.

**Change:** the no-dot case now builds the same tree the parser's own `do_float_split` builds in `crates/parser/src/shortcuts.rs`. The literal sits in an `ERROR` node and the open nodes are closed as in the dotted case.

I did not add the "illegal float literal" error message on the bridge side. The tree shape matches the parser, but that error won't appear for macro-expanded code.

`cargo test -p syntax-bridge -p parser` passes (8 and 320 tests), but none of them cover this input. A test that expands your `generate_field_accesses!(00E+10)` example would cover it.
